item.title: Adobe and Disney Team Up to Build AI Tools for the Next Generation of Storytelling (1 minute read)
item.description: Adobe has become Disney's Official AI Innovation Partner under a multi-year deal focused on storytelling, creativity, and responsible AI use. Adobe will give Disney early access to Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, and Photoshop, plus its own engineers and researchers. Through Firefly Foundry, Disney's models learn its characters and art styles, and Imagineering R&D already uses them to turn sketches into 2D concept art.

item.title: Instagram's Effect Builder Makes New Filters from AI Prompts (1 minute read)
item.description: Instagram's new Effect Builder, available now on the web to US residents over 18, turns AI prompts into custom Stories filters. Users can attach style reference images, preview effects on their own photos, and refine through follow-up prompts. An AI prompt-rewrite option adds paragraphs of style detail yet barely changes the result, and every effect must pass a safety review before others can use it.

item.title: Google Messages homepage redesign: Pinned chat avatars, bottom search, corner Gemini (3 minute read)
item.description: Google Messages is testing a redesigned Android homepage that displays pinned conversations as large contact avatars above the regular message list, similar to Apple's iMessage. Search moves from the top of the screen to a floating button near the bottom, alongside a new-chat button that changes shape while scrolling to improve one-handed usability. The Gemini shortcut also moves to the upper-right corner beside the profile image, with the changes currently rolling out selectively to beta testers.

item.title: When touch makes sense on a laptop (4 minute read)
item.description: Touchscreen laptops can make certain interactions faster than using a trackpad, particularly when selecting large targets or performing brief, direct actions. In a single-participant experiment across six tasks, touch averaged 1.39 seconds compared with 1.74 seconds for the trackpad, while previous research found similar advantages for some interactions. Touch remains less accurate for small targets and can cause fatigue during extended use, making it better suited as a complementary input method rather than a replacement for traditional laptop controls.

item.title: Making Immersive LLM Chat Experiences More Accessible (22 minute read)
item.description: Chat interfaces like Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini are interactive web content, so WCAG applies to them like any other page. A single live region announcing replies after streaming ends, hidden per-message headings, and sparing landmark use keep screen reader navigation workable. Skip links, Control+F6 shortcuts, user preferences, and research with disabled participants round out the approach.

item.title: Welcome to the Beige Era of Product Design. Here's Your Way Out (2 minute read)
item.description: Digital products are converging on the same look, driven by AI tools that repeat common solutions, vibe-design tools, shared UI libraries like shadcn/ui, and optimization culture. Convergence is "the floor," so designers should standardize what users expect. Borrowing automotive design's idea of "jewelry," teams should protect a few distinctive details, such as emotional moments like a first payment or a signed contract.

item.title: "x is dead" is dead (3 minute read)
item.description: Figma, wireframing, design files, and design systems aren't disappearing, but the standardized toolchains that once defined product design are fragmenting into increasingly personalized workflows. Designers now move between sketching tools, AI prompts, coding agents, and other applications, making it harder for organizations to enforce consistency through shared software alone. Design systems must therefore become tool-independent infrastructure that communicates not just components and tokens but also product principles, decision-making context, and the intentions behind design choices.

item.title: The Relationship between Visual Design and User Experience Design (17 minute read)
item.description: Visual design is only one part of UX, usually among the last decisions made, and it depends on an interdisciplinary team. Jesse James Garrett's five planes run from strategy through scope, structure, and skeleton to surface, where visual design sits. Continuous testing feeds back into decisions at every level.

item.title: Transform a Quick Drawing into a Live App with Gemini (1 minute read)

item.title: GitHub Previews a Redesigned Pull Request Overview (1 minute read)
item.description: GitHub's redesigned pull request Overview page began rolling out on November 5 as an opt-in public preview. A compact summary at the top now shows merge readiness, what is blocking it, and available actions, alongside new comment filters. Users can return to the classic view from the same menu. GitHub calls this an early iteration rather than the finished redesign.

item.title: Apple aiming to make Siri ‘more like an agent' as soon as next year: report (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple is reportedly working to transform Siri into a proactive AI agent capable of tracking goals, planning next steps, and completing tasks without requiring users to initiate every action. The company could introduce these capabilities as early as 2027, building on the personalized Siri features delivered with iOS 27 and potentially using its App Intents framework to interact with applications more efficiently. Apple is also adjusting its iOS 28 development process to give engineers more time for coding and experimentation, reflecting the growing influence of AI-assisted development.

item.title: Raising the ceiling must be earned (5 minute read)
item.description: AI tools can raise the baseline quality of creative work, but access to powerful technology does not automatically increase someone's ability to produce exceptional results. Developing taste and judgment requires understanding design fundamentals, recognizing weaknesses in generated work, and knowing how to direct improvements rather than accepting whatever looks convincing. AI-assisted prototyping can accelerate learning, but raising the ceiling of what's possible still depends on practicing the craft, understanding how things work, and developing the ability to critique them.

item.title: Why I Make Mood Boards (7 minute read)
item.description: Mood boards can become more than collections of visual references when the arrangement of images creates meanings that none of the individual pictures communicate alone. Juxtaposition, proximity, and contrast generate unexpected relationships between otherwise unrelated subjects, turning the act of collecting and arranging images into a form of visual thinking. Building collections gradually around themes such as machines, time, or technology allows new connections to emerge through experimentation rather than following a predetermined narrative.

item.title: No Figma, one branch, a 3-4 day sprint, and where the engineers take over (6 minute read)
item.description: Design engineers can shorten the distance between design and development by creating functional prototypes directly in a product's codebase instead of producing static Figma handoffs. In one team's workflow, a design engineer collaborates on discovery, builds and tests prototypes with users in three to four days, and delivers finished components with Storybook documentation while software engineers handle backend systems and architecture. The role combines front-end development, rapid prototyping, user research, and AI-assisted coding, allowing designers to contribute directly to production without replacing specialized engineering expertise.

item.title: There's No Better Name for Design Systems (4 minute read)
item.description: No better name for design systems exists, because what matters to stakeholders is what the system enables, not the components inside it. Product, methodology, and infrastructure each translate it for different audiences, with infrastructure traveling furthest across functions. Success means every team knows what the design system does for them, so it becomes simply the way things get built.

item.title: The volleyball World Cup logo looks... wrong (3 minute read)
item.description: The identity for the 2027 FIVB Men's Volleyball World Cup in Poland features an abstract white emblem inspired by the tournament trophy, surrounded by concentric red circles. Its design combines several symbolic references, including the trophy's silhouette, the Earth, a volleyball net, players reaching for a ball, and fans represented by a wave at the base. Although these elements are individually identifiable, their combination produces an ambiguous mark that raises questions about how much symbolism a logo can communicate before losing immediate visual clarity.

item.title: What greater devolution could mean for design (5 minute read)
item.description: Greater financial autonomy for regional governments in the UK could create new opportunities for design-led regeneration, with mayors gaining additional control over business rates, borrowing, and future income tax revenues. More predictable funding could encourage long-term investment in workplaces, infrastructure, and adaptive reuse projects that preserve local character while reducing construction waste and embodied carbon. Successful regeneration will depend on combining regional knowledge with broader design expertise, improving collaboration between public and private sectors, and creating spaces that reflect the communities and businesses they serve.

item.title: e.l.f.'s Stop-Motion Christmas Ad is a Win for Human Creativity (5 minute read)
item.description: e.l.f.'s first-ever holiday campaign is a stop-motion film built entirely by hand and narrated by Alan Cumming.

item.description: The Artphabet turns 26 famous artworks into 3D letters, from a Warhol soup can shaped like an A to Munch's The Scream bent into a Z.

item.title: Apple might be getting rid of the iPhone's Action button already (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple may remove the dedicated Action button from its 2027 iPhone lineup, merging its functionality with the existing Camera Control button as part of a broader redesign.

item.title: YouTube is giving its Android navigation bar a Liquid Glass-y makeover (2 minute read)
item.description: Google is testing a translucent floating bottom navigation bar in YouTube for Android, replacing the conventional attached navigation area with a design resembling Apple's Liquid Glass aesthetic. The experiment follows other recent navigation changes, including a separate test that removes the Subscriptions tab, and has prompted criticism that Google is borrowing from Apple's design language instead of following Material 3 Expressive. The new appearance appears to be controlled through a limited server-side experiment, with no official way to enable it manually.

item.title: ChatGPT can now turn your images into GIFs with its latest update (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Images 2.6 update introduces GIF generation across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, allowing static illustrations, characters, and product visuals to become short looping animations. Image generation is now up to 50% faster, with improved consistency across edits and two new API models: Flare for speed and Sunburst for higher-quality detail. Developers also gain image markup for targeted edits, SVG export, and controls for how much planning the model performs before generating an image.

item.title: Pangram, the Gold Standard for AI Text Checks, Releases Image 1.0 Tool to Sniff Fake Pics and Videos (2 minute read)
item.description: Pangram says Image 1.0 detected AI-generated pictures with 99.96% accuracy on its own evaluation set. The detector is available on the web, via API, and as a Chrome extension. Video detection runs on a lighter frame-by-frame model that scores 98.7% on the DF26 benchmark, ahead of TruthScan and Sightengine. Heatmaps show which parts of an image are AI-generated, and images as small as 256×256 pixels can be checked, with lower confidence below 512×512.

item.title: AI can generate the interface. What makes it worth caring about? (11 minute read)
item.description: AI can generate polished, consistent interfaces, but deciding when an experience should feel playful, surprising, celebratory, or restrained requires understanding the people and situations involved. A confetti animation might be appropriate after someone completes a major personal milestone but distracting when an administrator finishes a routine task for the forty-seventh time. Expressive design should therefore be evaluated for its purpose, context, accessibility, and potential to interrupt users rather than treated as decoration that makes every interaction more engaging.

item.title: How Figma Manages Sandboxes at Scale (9 minute read)
item.description: Figma's AI products, including its agent and Figma Make, need tens of thousands of sandboxes to run untrusted code safely. Nimbus, an internal platform, provisions, monitors, and routes those sandboxes across cloud providers through one simple API. Warm pools of pre-started sandboxes cut provisioning latency by about 90% and, together with automated provider selection, lifted provisioning availability from 99% to 99.95%.

item.title: Fortune Telling and Speculative Design (20 minute read)
item.description: Design engineers are particularly well positioned to explore possible futures because they combine visual design, software development, and the ability to build convincing working prototypes. Maggie Appleton's approach at GitHub Next involves collecting weak signals of emerging change, developing theories about where technology is heading, and creating tangible artifacts that make those possibilities easier to evaluate. Rather than trying to predict one inevitable future, speculative design helps teams investigate multiple plausible directions and make better decisions about what to build next.

item.title: Win the Demo, Lose the Market: Why Breakthrough Technology Isn't Enough (10 minute read)
item.description: Proterra delivered over 1,000 electric buses and grew revenue 24% in 2022, then filed for Chapter 11 the following year. Its buses worked, but below-cost pricing and order-by-order customization undid the business, because technical superiority is not the same as competitive advantage. Five shifts, from listing capabilities to defining consequences and from claims to proof, turn product advantage into enterprise advantage.

item.title: Tatiana Egoshina finds beauty in bad typography, Italian folklore and happy accidents (7 minute read)
item.description: Milan-based designer Tatiana Egoshina draws inspiration from unexpected everyday details, imperfect typography, and Italian folklore, transforming local stories and accidental discoveries into colorful identities, illustrations, and installations, including an award-winning projection onto the cliffs of southern Italy.

item.title: Major design IP reforms announced to tackle copycats, courtroom costs, and SUD protection (6 minute read)
item.description: The UK government has announced major reforms to design intellectual property protections aimed at making registration and enforcement fairer and more affordable for independent designers and small studios. Proposed changes would give the Intellectual Property Office stronger powers to reject copied or bad-faith registrations, addressing practices in which competitors register someone else's designs and use them to force legitimate products off online marketplaces. Registered design disputes would also become eligible for the Intellectual Property Enterprise Court's Small Claims Track, allowing creators to pursue claims of up to £10,000 without facing the substantial legal costs of conventional litigation.

item.title: These Classic Design Fails are Still Making Us Laugh (9 minute read)
item.description: Classic design fails, from Tesco's buttermilk carton to a UK government logo that looks rude when rotated 90 degrees, still raise plenty of laughs.

item.description: Halcyon Gallery in London hosts Johnny Depp's first major UK exhibition of original works, running from October 13 to November 15.

item.title: iPhone 18 will have two upgrades inspired by ‘Pro' models, per leak (2 minute read)
item.description: Apple's upcoming iPhone 18 will reportedly inherit two improvements from the iPhone 18 Pro: longer battery life and a more efficient processor. The new A20 chip is expected to use TSMC's 2-nanometer manufacturing process, potentially delivering significant performance and efficiency gains over previous generations. The standard model is expected in early 2027, but the smaller Dynamic Island will reportedly remain exclusive to Pro models, and a price increase is possible.

item.title: Figma Adds Google Drive and Internal Weave Tool Sharing (1 minute read)
item.description: Figma's agent and Make can now pull research, data, and images from Google Drive into a design conversation and create new Drive files. Connectors reach every plan, including Starter, though Google Drive is unavailable with the Governance+ add-on. Organization and Enterprise teams can also publish Weave tools internally, beside Figma's own and Community tools in the Tools tab.

item.title: Nubank unveils global brand refresh by Koto ahead of US launch (4 minute read)
item.description: Koto has refreshed Nubank's global identity ahead of its US expansion, creating a flexible brand system designed to accommodate more than 140 million customers and an expanding portfolio of financial products. The redesign retains the recognizable Nu logo while refining its signature purple, introducing proprietary Nu Sans Display and Nu Sans Text typefaces, and establishing a global library of photography, illustration, and motion assets. The system also extends into conversational AI, in-app animations built with Rive, and a redesigned global website, bringing greater consistency to Nubank's growing international presence.

item.title: Is this the most controversial font since Comic Sans? (3 minute read)
item.description: AI-generated posters are becoming recognizable through their repeated use of aggressive, upward-slanting brushstroke lettering, prompting comparisons with the much-maligned Comic Sans. ChatGPT attributes the repeated aesthetic to training data that associates oversized, distressed lettering with dramatic, attention-grabbing advertising and promotional graphics. Unlike Comic Sans, which was designed for a specific communication purpose, the AI-generated lettering often imitates expressive typography without understanding its context, turning a once-distinctive style into a visual cliché.

item.title: Design Feedback for AI Agents (3 minute read)
item.description: Design systems and agent instructions can guide AI-generated interfaces toward consistency, but they cannot anticipate every combination of components, layouts, and product states. A lightweight feedback loop helps close the remaining gap by letting designers annotate screenshots, comment in Figma, or provide spoken and written instructions that agents use to correct visual problems. Intent now integrates this workflow through a macOS screen-feedback feature, while human judgment remains essential for deciding which corrections should become reusable design system rules.

item.title: What does design system AI readiness mean, anyway? (12 minute read)
item.description: Making a design system AI-ready requires more than machine-readable documentation, design tokens, MCP servers, and agent skills. AI agents need constraints that guide them toward approved components, patterns, and implementation rules while reducing opportunities for inconsistent or invented solutions. The real measure of readiness is whether AI can participate in the design process without lowering quality, with human judgment remaining essential wherever tacit knowledge and context cannot be fully encoded.

item.title: “Designing a Good Poster is a Dark Art” – Highlights from This Year's INTL Poster Competition (8 minute read)
item.description: This year's INTL poster competition drew 2,670 entries from 78 countries, with 190 posters by more than 200 designers on display in Glasgow from November 12–22. Co-founder James Gilchrist calls a great poster near-impossible to design and singles out three trends: layered surfaces, 1990s-inspired collaged typography, and deliberately unprofessional, playful work.

item.title: Superior Type's Heaven is a sans serif built on oversized round shapes (3 minute read)
item.description: Superior Type's Heaven is a brutalist grotesque designed by Petr Kucera around oversized rounded shapes that appear compressed into rectangular spaces. The typeface includes four families, Heaven 01, 03, 06, and 09, each offering 18 styles from Thin to Black with italics, Latin and Cyrillic support, and a SuperVariable version that transitions from soft, rounded forms to boxier geometry. Distinctive curved letterforms, unconventional diagonals, and optional alternates give designers flexibility for expressive logos and display typography while retaining enough balance for longer text.

item.title: Designing a better future: your guide to design contribution in Open Source (12 minute read)
item.description: Open-source projects often lack the UX expertise needed to make powerful software approachable, while designers struggle to discover contribution opportunities in developer-oriented environments such as GitHub. Meaningful contributions can include user research, clearer project descriptions, onboarding improvements, navigation, error messages, accessibility, and better documentation of design processes rather than just visual assets. Designers can begin by exploring projects they already use, reviewing contribution guidelines, finding relevant issues, and collaborating directly with maintainers, even without extensive technical knowledge.

item.description: OpenAI is preparing to merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs into one experience, letting users move from discussing ideas to completing tasks with files, plugins, and web tools without switching tabs. The change will first reach select users for feedback, while Codex remains a separate section of the desktop app. ChatGPT and Codex share a token allowance, which could mean more frequent waits for usage resets for some users.

item.title: Canva Unveils Brush, an AI Model Built to Edit Designs at Lower Cost (5 minute read)
item.description: Brush, Canva's in-house vision-language model, edits designs up to 69% faster than the previous design agent at 46% lower cost per task. It reads both content and layout across full designs like multi-page decks, writes and runs small pieces of code, and inspects results before each next step. Brush is in beta for Canva Pro subscribers, with Brand Kit support and better image-heavy layout handling planned.

item.title: Amstel Updates Global Visual Identity to Highlight Amsterdam Heritage (2 minute read)
item.description: Amstel has redesigned its packaging and logo around its 1870 Amsterdam origins, adding bespoke typography inspired by historic canal bridge signage and a refined golden circle. The red, white, black, and gold system also features a wave pattern, a horizontal split evoking the Amstel River, and three coins representing the founders, city, and waterway. Already a Red Dot winner, the identity is rolling out across 11 markets, with all remaining territories due to transition by the end of 2027.

item.title: Design is more than creation (4 minute read)
item.description: Design is the deliberate process of deciding how something should work, respond, and be experienced, not simply the act of producing something that looks convincing. Conditions such as accessibility needs, localization, unpredictable content, failures, and different input methods should shape software from the beginning rather than being treated as edge cases to fix afterward. AI makes polished software dramatically faster to create, but that speed increases the importance of understanding which decisions were made, which assumptions they rely on, and whether they survive contact with reality.

item.title: How We're Training a Figma-Fluent Editing Model (4 minute read)
item.description: Specialized post-training lets Figma's first-party editing model compete with frontier models on precise, iterative edits to existing designs. A Llama 3.3 70B model trained on 250,000+ examples first became competitive with top models, but imitation learning limited generalization, so Figma now invests in reinforcement learning. Since beta, typical tasks run about 20% faster, users rate results 33% higher, and they undo the agent's work 60% less often.

item.title: Experience Design: Dropping the “User” from “User Experience” (6 minute read)
item.description: AI agents complicate the traditional definition of UX because people may increasingly accomplish goals without directly interacting with the companies, applications, and interfaces involved. Experience design provides a broader framing that includes traditional UX while also considering digital systems used by agents acting on humans' behalf and journeys involving multiple human and nonhuman actors. People's goals remain central, but designers must now consider experiences in which the immediate user of a product may be an AI rather than a person.

item.title: In the Age of AI, Curiosity is Our Greatest Creative Tool (7 minute read)
item.description: AI makes generating images and concepts easy, so the harder work is deciding what is worth making, whose perspective is missing, and whether it communicates. At DesignThinkers, RGD's annual conference in Toronto, speakers covered information design, blending strategy with creativity, and designing a city. AI-accelerated trends risk polished sameness, so "raw, messy curiosity is the most valuable thing we can bring to the table."

item.title: How to Write Better Copy for Graphic Design Projects (6 minute read)
item.description: Better graphic design copy starts with the project's purpose: a plain-language explanation, the audience, the most relevant benefit, objections, and the desired next step. Specific details persuade where vague praise does not, and a consistent brand voice should sound like the owner speaking face to face. Copy must fit its space, CTAs must match the reader's decision stage, and a final proofread should test every link and QR code.

item.title: Studio Kiln designs an identity for Reset that adapts like its app (4 minute read)
item.description: Studio Kiln's identity for Reset reflects the weight-loss app's personalized approach to eating, building flexibility and responsiveness directly into its visual system. A dynamic identity uses typography, color, imagery, and graphic elements that can shift across different contexts while maintaining a recognizable core. The result gives Reset a distinctive presence without locking a product built around personalized meal guidance into a rigid visual language.

item.title: The Window with No Buttons (9 minute read)
item.description: Style Dictionary, Storybook, and AI coding agents all run from the terminal, a blank window that feels like a wall to designers used to canvases.

item.title: French Concept Artist Uses Razor-Sharp Shapes and Neon Colors to Create the Most Dynamic Characters You Will See Today (1 minute read)
item.description: François Bourdin, a French freelance concept artist, character designer, and illustrator in Nantes, creates dynamic characters from razor-sharp angular linework and vivid, saturated neon palettes.

item.title: WhatsApp group chats get permanent message pins, private Status updates, and more (3 minute read)
item.description: WhatsApp is adding four features designed to make busy group conversations easier to manage, including permanent message pins and Group Status updates visible only to members of a particular group. A new filter collects unread conversations containing mentions, direct replies, or @all messages so users can quickly find messages that need their attention. Recent message history can also now be shared with someone after they have joined a group, helping new members catch up without exposing older conversations automatically.

item.title: Meta Quietly Launches an AI Fashion App Called Style Sketch (2 minute read)
item.description: Meta's Style Sketch is an AI app that builds a virtual closet from a user's Instagram photos and suggests outfits from clothes they already own. Virtual try-ons use a model reflecting the user's body shape and skin tone, and trip plans pack outfits around destination, activities, and weather. The app launched on iOS and Android in Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand, with no word on a wider rollout.

item.title: The iPad is Finally Getting the Affinity App Creatives Have Been Asking For (2 minute read)
item.description: Affinity's all-in-one creative app is finally coming to iPad, nearly a year after its desktop debut, answering long-standing demands since new-format files can't open in the older V2 iPad apps. It combines photo editing, vector design, page layout, and sketching, with Apple Pencil support for pressure, tilt, and barrel roll, plus RAW editing and formats like PSD, AI, INDD, and SVG. The app is free for individuals despite its “pre-order” label, though Canva AI Studio features require a premium plan.

item.title: “This wasn't a thoughtfully designed menu.” (4 minute read)
item.description: Hawaii's 2018 false missile alert demonstrates how poor information architecture, ambiguous labels, and insufficient friction can turn an interface mistake into a real-world emergency affecting 1.4 million people. The alert system reportedly placed confusingly named test and real commands together without clear hierarchy or confirmation proportional to the consequences, making a catastrophic selection surprisingly easy. The same principles apply to everyday software on a smaller scale: visually similar choices, weak labeling, and poorly structured menus create countless small errors that gradually erode usability and trust.

item.title: There Will Always Be Someone Faster, Cheaper, and Better (8 minute read)
item.description: AI intensifies designers' fears about competing with people who can work faster, cheaper, or better, but those pressures have existed throughout the history of professional design and every major shift in production tools. Faster tools become threatening when designers price their time rather than outcomes, while “better” extends beyond the quality of an artifact to the experience, perspective, judgment, and relationships a designer brings to a client. As AI makes production faster, deliberately taking time to gain experience, make mistakes, and develop a singular way of working may become more valuable than racing to master whichever tool is currently dominant.

item.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)
item.description: Slow design system components make every app built on them slow, so performance belongs next to accessibility on the team's priority list. Timing ten popular systems on a 249-country dropdown and 100 checkboxes found Fluent and Carbon quickest to open the dropdown and Ionic by far the slowest. Playwright tests with explicit budgets, virtualized long lists, and published performance numbers keep components fast by default.

item.title: Automate Video Creation with AI Agent (Website)
item.description: An AI video agent that turns your ideas, documents, links, and media assets into share-ready videos. Describe the video you want to make, upload your assets, and Cutbay helps you shape the idea.

item.title: A Library of Patterns and Principles for Inventing New Interfaces (Website)
item.description: An interlinked library that takes interfaces apart for the people who make them. Every entry names the mechanism, traces it back to the people who built it, and connects it to the ideas it grew from.

item.title: Free Online PDF Accessibility Checker (Website)
item.description: Check the accessibility of your PDF against WCAG and PDF/UA. Get actionable recommendations to fix the issues and move toward ADA, Section 508, and EAA compliance.

item.title: Website Design that Converts: Why Good-Looking Sites Still Fail (4 minute read)
item.description: Striking photography wins attention but fails when visitors cannot tell what working with a studio involves. Dutch lighting consultancy Eclectic Lighting bridges that gap with sector-based project filters, a four-step process, specific client reviews, and a floor plan upload. Asking for a floor plan visitors already have turns the contact form into a concrete next step.

item.title: COPUS and Kontrapunkt design JUNO the bakery's cookie brand and site (4 minute read)
item.description: Kontrapunkt extended Copenhagen's JUNO the bakery into a restrained identity and packaging system built around white paper, subtle blue accents, simple duotone illustrations, and the bakery's blue peacock mascot. Its Danish Butter Cookies use the same quiet visual language. COPUS and Tommy Campbell carried the identity into JUNO's first online shop, using blue sparingly for highlights, product tiles, and the add-to-cart button to make the digital experience feel like a window into the physical bakery.

item.title: I Gave My Website a Boss Fight (11 minute read)
item.description: Missing the personality of the old internet, Paul Bakaus rebuilt his personal website over ten days with Claude Code as a retro Amiga-style world, using a 4,096-color palette, live-synthesized music, and a boss fight against a monster called Jirasaurus. Each page became a themed scene, from a rooftop panel and a speaking auditorium to a floppy-disk office platformer, and three pages hide playable games. Claude wrote the code, built the art pipeline, and composed the music, but animation needed a leg rig and constant feedback, and the site stays a fast, optional-to-play Ghost theme where reading still comes first.

item.title: This Horse-Shaped Headset Asks Designers to See the World Through Animal Eyes (6 minute read)
item.description: Equine Eyes, an oversized horse-head headset, uses side-mounted cameras and a VR display to simulate a horse's nearly 350-degree field of view and blue-yellow color perception.

item.title: This Artist is Using 90s Anime Aesthetics to Create the Ultimate Nostalgic Masterpieces That Will Hit You Right in the Feels (1 minute read)
item.description: Japanese-American illustrator Mike Yoshimura channels 80s and 90s anime, retro cyberpunk, and vintage cel animation into solitary figures in neon-lit rain and twilight cityscapes.

item.title: How this artist turned childhood nightmares into video game monsters (6 minute read)
item.description: John Kenn Mortensen translated his hand-drawn creatures and childhood fascination with darkness into the fantasy roguelike FLASK, combining grotesque medieval imagery, black humor, Labyrinth-like fantasy, and the energy of Slayer while working with a game art team to preserve his distinctive style in a colorful digital world.
